name: GPS Spoofing
Description: An attack where fraudulent GPS signals are broadcasted to deceive the drone's GPS receiver, leading it to calculate an incorrect position, altitude, or velocity.
Symptoms: Sudden coordinate shifts (telemetry jumps) without corresponding inertial movement
High Horizontal Dilution of Precision (HDOP) or vertical accuracy metric anomalies
Discrepancies between GPS-derived position and onboard sensor fusion (inertial navigation, optical flow, or LIDAR)
Abrupt changes in the reported number of visible satellites or signal-to-noise ratios (SNR)
Impact: Can result in the drone navigating off-course, colliding with obstacles, flying into restricted airspace, experiencing fly-away scenarios, or being hijacked to an attacker-designated landing zone.
Recommended Action: Enable GPS verification modules. Immediately transition the flight controller from GPS-dependent modes to inertial navigation (dead reckoning) or manual control. Command the drone to hover in place, or initiate a safe non-GPS auto-landing.
